proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived atom-unrestricted, no-grid known-propensity regret bounds, a conditional DR oracle inequality, overlap-sharp converse witnesses, and exact constants in the balanced two-policy experiment. Both review panels passed, all seven cited leaves were independently source-attested, and the graph has no open statements. The package remains subfield against the field floor (score 6.5 versus 7.4); preserve it for a deliberate reanchor, with partial-result prose needing editorial reconciliation and no Lean formalization attempted.
tldr: For the fixed causal population-barycenter welfare \(U_P\), an observable projected IPW selector attains the atom-unrestricted, no-log, overlap-sharp expected-regret order \(\min\{1,\sqrt{V/(n\epsilon)}\}\). The published Lipschitz class already supplies the matching converse through Huang et al., Theorem 12; an additional equal-mean two-atom jump family has the same order. In the separate balanced constant-context experiment with two constant policies, the exact asymptotic minimax constants are \(\lambda\) for the full class and \(\kappa/2\) for the shape class, with \(\lambda>\kappa/2\); the observable randomized radial selector attains \(\lambda\). A separate cross-fitted DR inequality retains population \(L^2\) nuisance-product bias and foldwise conditional centered-process errors. Huang receives credit for the quantile geometry and lower-rate mechanism, and Athey--Wager for weighted VC tools.
gap: The inspected specialized upper theorem requires quantile regularity, which fails for empirical distributions with separated support points.
fill: Integrate a weighted scalar VC second-moment bound in quantile space and apply Hilbert projection to obtain the expected-regret order \(\min\{1,\sqrt{V/n}\}\). Separate DR bias from foldwise conditional fluctuations and test the sharpness of the shape-only witness through the open constant comparison.
